What a /7 means

A /7 holds 33,554,432 addresses and is only seen as a large provider or registry aggregate.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /7 uses 7 network bits and leaves 25 host bits, so the block contains 33,554,432 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−7) − 2 = 33,554,432 − 2 = 33,554,430.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 0.0.0.1 254.0.0.0
!
access-list 10 permit 0.0.0.0 1.255.255.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 0.0.0.1/7

Linux

ip addr add 0.0.0.1/7 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /7?

33,554,430. A /7 has 33,554,432 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 33,554,430 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /7?

254.0.0.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 1.255.255.255.
